commits.summary: Split examples into demo/ and real-world/, with Commons Numbers #223 as the first real-world example
commits.body: The 56 numbered examples, the four subject systems (apps/), the generator and the Java verifier (tools/), schema/ and index.json moved from examples/ to examples/demo/, and examples/real-world/ was added for pull requests to published libraries verified with the /verify-bytecode skill: a README with the verified pull requests and the table of libraries to try next (moved out of the plugin README), and commons-numbers-223/, a record of the run on apache/commons-numbers#223 (ArithmeticUtils.pow) with the witness, the four verdicts and their times as recorded on 2026-11-01, what the run did not reach (pow(long, int), the module-level diffs), how it was produced (the file compiled alone with javac because the Maven build could not run in that session), and the commands to rerun it. examples/README.md is now a short hub for the two kinds; approaches.md and setup/ stay shared. The root README, the lib README, the plugin READMEs and references, lib's tests and doc comments, and every path inside the examples (patches, example.json, result.json, SARIF, verifier output, contract headers) point at the new paths; build.py's repo root and link depth were adjusted.

commits.summary: Run the feature loop seven times on TLA examples
commits.body:
feature-loop.sh used to repeat its instruction until a cycle made no commit. It now runs a fixed number of cycles (CYCLES=7) and exits 0 after the last one, and the instruction is now to add more advanced examples showcasing verification of TLA specs. The old instruction is replaced, not queued after the new one. A cycle with no commit still stops the loop early with exit 1, before compacting. The README describes the limit.

Verified by running the real script, including its memory scope, with a stub claude in a temporary jj repo: seven commits gave seven instructions and seven compacts, all with the new text, and exit 0; no commit on the third cycle gave three instructions, two compacts and exit 1. The loop has not been run against the real session.

commits.summary: Choose the feature loop's prompt by argument
commits.body:
feature-loop.sh now takes the name of a prompt: features is the earlier instruction to add features and examples to jvmcontract, with no limit on cycles as before, and tla is the instruction to add advanced TLA examples, seven times. Each run takes exactly one name; anything else prints the usage and exits 2 before the memory scope starts. The argument is passed through the re-execution into the scope. The README shows both.

Verified by running the real script, including its memory scope, with a stub claude in a temporary jj repo: tla gave seven instructions, seven compacts and exit 0; features ran past seven cycles until a cycle made no commit at the tenth, then exit 1, with its own text; no argument, an unknown name and two names each gave exit 2 without calling claude. The loop has not been run against the real session.
